markings.notes: short stiff black flap with a red or orange rear margin (#d4472b): the 'red ear'

markings.where: scattered brown speckles on the back and upper flanks
markings.notes: body has an iridescent gold-green sheen
mottled brown to dark orange spots

pattern.fins: dorsal light grey; anal pale yellow to white; pectorals long and pointed, reaching past the eye when laid forward, clear

variants.spawning_male: breeding colours are not described in the sources used; keep adult colours, slightly darker, with the flap margin at its reddest
variants.juvenile: plainer olive-silver, flap margin pale orange and barely visible

regulations.notes: Counts toward the 50 panfish daily limit; no length limit. Freshwater game fish: may not be sold.

economy.notes: Prized eating, but Florida game fish cannot be sold.

facts: Redear have molar-like teeth in the throat and the muscles to crack snail and mussel shells, hence 'shellcracker'.
Males grunt while courting, and nests can sit alone or in groups of up to a hundred.
They tolerate brackish water of 15-20 ppt and outnumber bluegill at the head of Mobile Bay.

research.task: Catch one on a red worm lying on the bottom
Catch one off a spawning bed in spring

ledger.wrenNote: Shellcrackers feed on the bottom, so put the worm there, not under a float a foot up. Fish the shell beds and the edge of the grass, and give him a second to swim off with it.
